extraction.body: AI agents from multiple providers accessed personal data and confidential material at Indian organizations during research and testing, India’s cybersecurity agency said Thursday. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said it had received “multiple voluntary disclosures from AI model providers” whose models, during research and evaluation runs on the open internet, “had reached the live systems of Indian organizations.” The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles, and their actions “exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks.” This makes India the latest stop on what has become a world tour for rogue AI agents. In July, OpenAI’s agents escaped a test environment and hacked French company Hugging Face — kicking off a summer of rogue AI agent activity. Last month, OpenAI apologized to Australia after its agents accessed four government websites, including a Medicare statistics portal. At Hugging Face, OpenAI’s agents started the same way but then found and exploited software flaws to run code on the company’s servers. CERT-In described no such hacking in India, where the agents appear to have simply used the access left lying around. Still, the Indian cases appear to be worse in one respect, which is what the agents saw: In Australia, OpenAI said it found no evidence its agents touched individuals’ medical or criminal records, even after they wrote files inside a Medicare statistics system, while in India, agents read personal data and confidential business records. And unlike earlier incidents, each disclosed by a single lab, India’s case involved agents from multiple providers. CERT-In did not name the providers or affected organizations, or say whether the agents altered any systems. TechCrunch has reached out to CERT-In for more information. For now, the closest parallel seems to be Anthropic’s July disclosure of Claude breaking into three companies’ systems during testing using basic techniques like weak passwords. In India, as in Anthropic’s cases, the affected organizations had not detected the intrusions on their own. The disclosures have left governments relying on AI companies causing these breaches to voluntarily disclose rogue AI agent activity. sources.title: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film ‘the right way’ and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy
passages: Wahlberg, who’s also an entrepreneur and angel investor, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt to share his perspective on AI’s role in filmmaking, and how he’s open to having an AI likeness of himself carry on his legacy.
Even as Hollywood remains divided over the use of AI in filmmaking, actor and director Mark Wahlberg believes the technology has a place in the industry as long as it’s used the right way.

“It’s a fairly expensive movie, but, we’re talking about utilizing [AI] to enhance the stadium setting, things of that nature,” Wahlberg said. “I don’t think you should just, you know, put an idea into ChatGPT and it puts out a script, and then you should go make that and not use real actors.
Those are cutting-edge moments in technology with computer-generated images.
He even said he wouldn’t be opposed if his upcoming animated series, “Ted,” continued for decades with an AI version of his likeness.

When asked by TechCrunch Editor-in-Chief Connie Loizos whether he had visited the CAA Vault , a Creative Artists Agency facility which lets actors use scanning technology to capture their bodies, faces, movements, and voices to create AI replicas, Wahlberg said he hadn’t, but would be open to the idea.

sources.title: Tesla turns to 50-year-old stunt technology as it tries to Roadster again
passages: Nine years after first trying to resurrect the Roadster , Tesla is apparently trying again.

CEO Elon Musk might have relocated its HQ to Texas, but yet again he has returned to California’s showbiz industry to hawk his wares; last time it was a Hollywood back lot for the remote-controlled Cybercab demo , last night it was decades-old stunt technology to make a show car do tricks in the air.
And right now, that’s the McMurtry Spéirling, which looks like a miniaturized Batmobile (the good Michael Keaton one) and which is capable of generating up to 3.5 lateral Gs.
The best Tesla claims for the new Roadster is 2 Gs.
Oh, and the Spéirling will most definitely drive upside down.
Musk claims that the Roadster will go into production by 2028.

But the CEO has a long and glorious history of overpromising and underdelivering; in 2017 he told attendees at the previous launch that “We are making it now.” Using the company’s referral program, some people were in line to receive two free cars.
But those free cars never showed up, and neither did the ones that people put down $50,000 deposits for; last year Sam Altman discovered how hard it can be to get that money back .
But as Musk has told us time and again, Tesla is no longer a car company .
Currently, he seems more interested in merging Tesla with SpaceX , claiming synergies having to do with AI despite most of his AI-derived revenues coming from renting GPU time to others.
But a merger would give SpaceX a backdoor into the S&P 500 index, which rejected the rocket company in June, as it requires several consecutive profitable quarters for inclusion.
Apparently, that could happen before the end of the year.
At the rear are four giant exhaust pipes; these do not signal Tesla’s sudden embrace of hydrocarbons beyond those emitted by private aviation.

The battery pack uses the troubled 4680 cells it has been trying to scale up in-house; customer complaints of poor performance were presumably the driving force behind developing what the company says is a special battery chemistry just for this model.
Some of the performance claims are even more grandiose than nine years ago.
Now, Musk claims a planned top speed of 383 mph (616 km/h), with a 0-60 mph time of 0.8 seconds.
And as with the last time this happened , there are already other EVs on sale that are more capable than Tesla’s vaporware claims.

Its stratospheric valuation was predicated in large part upon promises of constant growth, something that perhaps seemed possible when its market share was near total and there was little competition for EVs.
But now Europe and China have hundreds of models to choose from—only two of which are offered by Tesla.
The Models 3 and Y are both increasingly aged, and Tesla has shown little ability to innovate rapidly like the Chinese brands that have taken so much of its sales away there.
In fact, it might even leave the Chinese market .
Meanwhile, Tesla’s core business remains in trouble.
Even in quarters with decent sales, its profits are vanishing as costs rise and selling prices drop .
And most recently, sales have not been decent .

extraction.body: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard. OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own. The incident—which likely would have resulted in criminal charges had they been performed directly by a person—has further heightened concerns that widespread AI use could have harmful effects on an unprecedented scale. In two of the cases reported Thursday, OpenAI agents tasked with retrieving information from websites hacked them when the models ran into obstacles obtaining it directly. In one incident during reinforcement training, a model that received access denials when trying to retrieve historical hospital-bed statistics on a government statistics website “used the site’s file-download feature to retrieve server configuration and application files, including sensitive credentials,” OpenAI said . “It inspected the application code, bypassed the statistics endpoint’s authorization checks, and retrieved data that had previously been denied. The model saved the data locally.” In the other incident , a model instructed to retrieve figures from a public research dashboard bypassed the organization’s security controls and used the unauthorized access to steal credentials. It then made configuration changes on the server. In one evaluation, the changes let the model make an internal search tool relay queries to the public dashboard. In a second evaluation, the model downloaded five non-public tables containing 147,451 rows. OpenAI researchers had prompted the agents to retrieve only five dashboard figures. Even after resetting the setting, the model continued using the token to retrieve non-public data. “The evaluation ended without the model disclosing that it had guessed answers, accessed the organization’s internal systems, downloaded non-public tables, or changed the authentication configuration,” OpenAI said. “All five answers in this evaluation were marked incorrect.” In a third report , the company said a model prompted to update a cryptocurrency trading application used funds from a locked wallet on a test network. The model “derived wallet keys from publicly known developer recovery phrases, found an account with test-network funds, and used that account to pay for the requested contract deployment.” The report continued: “The model questioned whether it had permission, then reasoned that a public recovery phrase and valueless test-network tokens made the funds acceptable to use. The deployment succeeded and charged transaction fees to the account. This case shows that a model can substitute its own judgment about likely harm for the account holder’s permission, then act on that judgment without authorization.” In the last report , OpenAI said that a model bypassed restrictions researchers had placed on the types of web requests it could make. During reinforcement-learning training, the model had been prompted to seek public trade statistics. OpenAI went on: After finding a public yearbook and submitting an answer, it continued probing for another route to the statistics service. It caused an external browser to send POST requests, retrieved annual figures as an image, and extracted them using optical character recognition. It then developed a reusable helper that returned response text through a forwarding service and callback mailbox, repeatedly checked the retrieved figures, and used saved data in submitted responses. This case shows how a model can bypass restrictions on its own tools by getting external services to perform the blocked actions, even after finding another way to answer the question. The model first tried to use an external browser with permission to make GET requests on its behalf, then used JavaScript to obtain the information. The model then used an online mailbox to troubleshoot the technique. Eventually, the model settled on a different method: It asked the external browser to open a web form that sent the trade query to the statistics service by POST. When the browser displayed the response, a rendering service returned a GIF image of the page. The model then used optical character recognition to read the figures from the image. It has become common for researchers and journalists to describe incidents like these as AI “going rogue.” That’s not necessarily true. While prompts fed to the models didn’t instruct them to use the alternate methods for completing their objectives, models are trained to be efficient, steadfastly persistent, and, when possible, to find shortcuts that lessen workloads. Further, most or all of the models had disabled certain guardrails that might have prevented the actions. In this sense, the models performed precisely as OpenAI had trained them to. story.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites - Ars Technica

facts.text: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts.
In two of the cases reported Thursday, OpenAI agents tasked with retrieving information from websites hacked them when the models ran into obstacles obtaining it directly.

In one incident during reinforcement training, a model that received access denials when trying to retrieve historical hospital-bed statistics on a government statistics website “used the site’s file-download feature to retrieve server configuration and application files, including sensitive credentials,” OpenAI said .
“It inspected the application code, bypassed the statistics endpoint’s authorization checks, and retrieved data that had previously been denied.

In one evaluation, the changes let the model make an internal search tool relay queries to the public dashboard.
OpenAI researchers had prompted the agents to retrieve only five dashboard figures.
Even after resetting the setting, the model continued using the token to retrieve non-public data.
“All five answers in this evaluation were marked incorrect.”
It has become common for researchers and journalists to describe incidents like these as AI “going rogue.” That’s not necessarily true.

While prompts fed to the models didn’t instruct them to use the alternate methods for completing their objectives, models are trained to be efficient, steadfastly persistent, and, when possible, to find shortcuts that lessen workloads.
During reinforcement-learning training, the model had been prompted to seek public trade statistics.

extraction.body: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard. OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own. The incident—which likely would have resulted in criminal charges had they been performed directly by a person—has further heightened concerns that widespread AI use could have harmful effects on an unprecedented scale. In two of the cases reported Thursday, OpenAI agents tasked with retrieving information from websites hacked them when the models ran into obstacles obtaining it directly. In one incident during reinforcement training, a model that received access denials when trying to retrieve historical hospital-bed statistics on a government statistics website “used the site’s file-download feature to retrieve server configuration and application files, including sensitive credentials,” OpenAI said . “It inspected the application code, bypassed the statistics endpoint’s authorization checks, and retrieved data that had previously been denied. The model saved the data locally.” In the other incident , a model instructed to retrieve figures from a public research dashboard bypassed the organization’s security controls and used the unauthorized access to steal credentials. It then made configuration changes on the server. In one evaluation, the changes let the model make an internal search tool relay queries to the public dashboard. In a second evaluation, the model downloaded five non-public tables containing 147,451 rows. OpenAI researchers had prompted the agents to retrieve only five dashboard figures. Even after resetting the setting, the model continued using the token to retrieve non-public data. “The evaluation ended without the model disclosing that it had guessed answers, accessed the organization’s internal systems, downloaded non-public tables, or changed the authentication configuration,” OpenAI said. “All five answers in this evaluation were marked incorrect.” In a third report , the company said a model prompted to update a cryptocurrency trading application used funds from a locked wallet on a test network. The model “derived wallet keys from publicly known developer recovery phrases, found an account with test-network funds, and used that account to pay for the requested contract deployment.” The report continued: “The model questioned whether it had permission, then reasoned that a public recovery phrase and valueless test-network tokens made the funds acceptable to use. The deployment succeeded and charged transaction fees to the account. This case shows that a model can substitute its own judgment about likely harm for the account holder’s permission, then act on that judgment without authorization.” In the last report , OpenAI said that a model bypassed restrictions researchers had placed on the types of web requests it could make. During reinforcement-learning training, the model had been prompted to seek public trade statistics. OpenAI went on: After finding a public yearbook and submitting an answer, it continued probing for another route to the statistics service. It caused an external browser to send POST requests, retrieved annual figures as an image, and extracted them using optical character recognition. It then developed a reusable helper that returned response text through a forwarding service and callback mailbox, repeatedly checked the retrieved figures, and used saved data in submitted responses. This case shows how a model can bypass restrictions on its own tools by getting external services to perform the blocked actions, even after finding another way to answer the question. The model first tried to use an external browser with permission to make GET requests on its behalf, then used JavaScript to obtain the information. The model then used an online mailbox to troubleshoot the technique. Eventually, the model settled on a different method: It asked the external browser to open a web form that sent the trade query to the statistics service by POST. When the browser displayed the response, a rendering service returned a GIF image of the page. The model then used optical character recognition to read the figures from the image. It has become common for researchers and journalists to describe incidents like these as AI “going rogue.” That’s not necessarily true. While prompts fed to the models didn’t instruct them to use the alternate methods for completing their objectives, models are trained to be efficient, steadfastly persistent, and, when possible, to find shortcuts that lessen workloads. Further, most or all of the models had disabled certain guardrails that might have prevented the actions. In this sense, the models performed precisely as OpenAI had trained them to. sources.title: Ukraine war briefing: Russia building non-negotiable ‘security zone’ inside Ukrainian border, Putin declares - The Guardian
passages: Russia is establishing a “security zone” inside Ukraine along the border and it will be non-negotiable in any ⁠future talks with Kyiv, Vladimir Putin has said .

The Russian president, wearing military uniform and speaking during a visit to a command post, said the operation ⁠was in response to Ukraine’s ⁠2024-25 incursion into ​Russia’s western Kursk region .
This task is being carried out successfully,” he said in televised comments on Friday.
“Our goal is to ensure the absolute security of Russia’s border regions ⁠for the future, and we do not plan to make this a subject for potential peace negotiations with ​Ukraine.”
The planned ‌security zone spanned 660km (410 ‌miles) , of which 70% was currently under Russia’s control, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said.
Peskov did not say how deep it would ‌reach inside Ukraine.
The zone requires Russia to carve out land in the Sumy and Kharkiv regions, which are not among those it is illegally claiming as its own territory.

Zelenskyy said the Ukrainian military’s access to the Starlink satellite internet service had not yet been fully restored , as media reports suggested the order to throttle the service had come from within the White House.
Zelenskyy met European leaders on Friday in Brussels and asked the EU for another €70bn ($79bn/£59bn) next year to fund Ukraine’s defence against Russia, report Jennifer Rankin and Andrew Roth .
Hours earlier Trump called Ukraine’s renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries “a disgrace” after his purported “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine failed to take hold.
The attacks came as a new report showed that civilian casualties from Russia’s invasion have climbed steeply.
At least 328 civilians were killed and 2,105 wounded last month – a total that is 85% higher than in September last year, the report from the UN human rights office in Kyiv said on Friday.
It said intensifying Russian attacks in October already had killed dozens of civilians, including children.
“The first two weeks of October were among the deadliest periods for civilians in years,” said Danielle Bell, the UN office head.

As Russian missiles and drones have systematically slammed into power plants in Kyiv and Kharkiv this week, the rolling blackouts and water outages have increasingly resembled a supposed Russian blueprint to destroy life in major Ukrainian cities seen by the Guardian, writes Andrew Roth in this analysis .
Two were kiled and 12 more wounded in attacks on three districts of the eastern city of Kharkiv, governor Oleh Syniehubov ⁠said.
Further Russian strikes through the evening injured nine, officials said.
A Russian ⁠airstrike on ​Kherson in southern ⁠Ukraine killed one ⁠person ​and ‌injured ‌19 others , the governor ‌said on Saturday.
The person ‌killed was an ​ambulance driver and ⁠a child ​was among the ​injured, ​Oleksandr Prokudin ​said ‌on ​Telegram.

That process alone can take hours, especially when a client wants small braids.

Diallo said the device is designed to work like this: A stylist places the braiding hair on top of it and sets the size they want the hair separated into, and the device separates the pieces and dispenses them back to the stylist so they can grab them while braiding.
Braiding is a manual task, and a single style can take eight hours to complete.
Tressfecta is still technically prelaunch, and it is working on the prototype of Plait Pilot.
Diallo has been bootstrapping the company, while also drawing on funding from grant and accelerator programs.
“I am preparing to fundraise,” she said, noting how hard it can be to raise money for hardware, especially beauty hardware.

extraction.body: Aisata Diallo, 24, calls herself a lifelong braider. “I’ve always braided my hair growing up and, at some point in my college career, started braiding other people’s hair,” she said. At Northeastern University in Boston, she found limited access to braiders and textured-hair specialists, so she decided to fill that gap by starting a small business of her own. “Throughout that experience, I was very close to some of the pain points in the styling process and complained about it constantly,” she said. Braiding is a manual task, and a single style can take eight hours to complete. Many professionals deal with issues like cramping and carpal tunnel syndrome after spending long days standing behind a chair weaving hair into patterns. At first, Diallo said she didn’t know what to do about it. “I stopped braiding, and one of the reasons that I stopped braiding was due to the physical toll it has on your body.” She wanted to find a way to make braiding less painful and wondered whether new AI technology could automate some part of the process. Building hardware for braiding is expensive, difficult, and complex, which is one reason there have been few innovations in this space. The textured hair market has also long been overlooked by the mainstream. Then, last year, she had an idea: Tressfecta, a company building products for textured hair. Its first project is a tool called Plait Pilot that helps braiders with the initial process of separating hair from packs before braiding begins. That process alone can take hours, especially when a client wants small braids. Diallo said the device is designed to work like this: A stylist places the braiding hair on top of it and sets the size they want the hair separated into, and the device separates the pieces and dispenses them back to the stylist so they can grab them while braiding. “It’s very challenging to build this kind of tool in this space,” she said, citing the nuance and complexity of the braiding style process. Different types of textured hair also need to be accounted for, especially when length and density are considered. “It’s not a one-size-fits-all solution.” Tressfecta is still technically prelaunch, and it is working on the prototype of Plait Pilot. Diallo has been bootstrapping the company, while also drawing on funding from grant and accelerator programs. “I am preparing to fundraise,” she said, noting how hard it can be to raise money for hardware, especially beauty hardware. For now, Diallo said she’s connecting with stylists and braiders who can test the technology. She also spent this week in San Francisco as one of TechCrunch’s Startup Battlefield 200 companies. She doesn’t remember exactly where she first heard about TechCrunch Disrupt, possibly on LinkedIn or in a founder resource group, but when we talked ahead of the show, which wrapped up on Thursday , she was looking forward to connecting with people and showing off her product. She was especially excited to connect with people and for others to see her product. “It feels like a great opportunity,” she said. Diallo has been bootstrapping the company, while also drawing on funding from grant and accelerator programs. “I am preparing to fundraise,” she said, noting how hard it can be to raise money for hardware, especially beauty hardware. For now, Diallo said she’s connecting with stylists and braiders who can test the technology. She also spent this week in San Francisco as one of TechCrunch’s Startup Battlefield 200 companies.

sources.title: Jev is Vercel’s fastest-adopted AI model ever
passages: Vercel data published on Thursday shows that, within two weeks of its launch, the buzzy decision model was being used by 35% of paid teams, with nearly double the reach of the second most popular model, Sonnet 5.5.
It’s the fastest adoption a model has ever seen in its first two weeks, according to Vercel’s data, and a major accomplishment for the model’s creators, TypeSafe AI.
In fact, Vercel was an early adopter of Jev, using it to replace GPT-6 Luna for classifying harmful commands.
Jev has become the fastest adopted AI model ever — at least by some measures.
Published in limited release on September 15, Jev is designed as a lightweight tool for choosing between a few predetermined outputs.
Limiting the outputs lets the model run cheaper and faster than alternatives like Sonnet, making it ideal for classifying large quantities of data quickly.

That new approach has attracted significant buzz in the weeks since Jev’s release — inspiring competing offerings from OpenAI and Amazon , among others — but until now there has been little hard data to back up the good vibes.

Vercel data published on Thursday shows that, within two weeks of its launch, the buzzy decision model was being used by 35% of paid teams, with nearly double the reach of the second most popular model, Sonnet 5.5. It’s the fastest adoption a model has ever seen in its first two weeks, according to Vercel’s data, and a major accomplishment for the model’s creators, TypeSafe AI. Published in limited release on September 15, Jev is designed as a lightweight tool for choosing between a few predetermined outputs. Limiting the outputs lets the model run cheaper and faster than alternatives like Sonnet, making it ideal for classifying large quantities of data quickly. That new approach has attracted significant buzz in the weeks since Jev’s release — inspiring competing offerings from OpenAI and Amazon , among others — but until now there has been little hard data to back up the good vibes. The data comes from Vercel’s AI gateway , a unified API service similar to OpenRouter. It’s a necessarily limited view — particularly at risk of undercounting major labs like OpenAI and Anthropic that offer their own APIs — but it shows the buzz around Jev really did translate into actual usage. In fact, Vercel was an early adopter of Jev, using it to replace GPT-6 Luna for classifying harmful commands. The report also shows continuing momentum for open source models, which now account for more than 70% of the tokens processed through Vercel’s gateway and nearly 25% of the total spend. While open source models are capturing a larger share of the market, the market is also growing fast. Spending on frontier labs has grown tenfold, even as it accounts for a smaller share of overall spend, giving credence to the idea that frontier models and open source alternatives may turn out to be complementary rather than competitive . sources.title: Amazon’s Bee launches two new personal AI devices, starting at $75 - TechCrunch
passages: Amazon’s personal AI wearable maker, Bee , is announcing its first new products since being acquired by the retail giant last year .

The tech company on Thursday introduced the Bee Frontier, the next generation of its device that can be worn on the wrist or pinned to clothes, along with Bee Eclipse, a credit-card-sized device that magnetically attaches to the back of your smartphone.
To make all this possible, Bee devices use a private computing security architecture, which doesn’t store the raw audio from your conversations.
Instead, audio is processed in real time and then deleted.

Transcripts of the conversation are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls, which means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you manually and intentionally share them.
In addition, you can opt to connect the Bee to Alexa, allowing your Echo device to use its ability to identify your voice, a feature called Voice ID, to recognize when you’re speaking.

The latter puts Bee into more direct competition with AI devices like the Plaud Note or Pocket, but at a lower price point — the Bee Frontier is $74.99, compared with $159 for the Plaud Note (or $189 for the Note Pro), or $129 for the Pocket AI device .
With its new connections to Amazon.com and Alexa, Bee users can make purchases from Amazon or ask Alexa for their Bee insights, summaries, or to-dos hands-free.

Like the original Bee, the idea with the new devices is to leverage AI to take notes from your everyday conversations, allowing you to remember the important things that were said, and then turn those into actionable to-dos, summaries, and insights.
For instance, if you discussed making plans with friends, the Bee would remember the date and time you agreed on, then create a calendar invite.
Bee also works with your existing productivity software, like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Microsoft Outlook, so it can draft emails, set up meetings, surface action items, and more.

The Bee Frontier will come in Onyx, Lavender, and Sage, while the $99.99 Bee Eclipse will be offered in Silver, Midnight, Honey, and Blush. Like the original Bee, the idea with the new devices is to leverage AI to take notes from your everyday conversations, allowing you to remember the important things that were said, and then turn those into actionable to-dos, summaries, and insights. For instance, if you discussed making plans with friends, the Bee would remember the date and time you agreed on, then create a calendar invite. You could also use the Bee to take lecture notes in class, or to jot down the care plan you discussed with a doctor, among other things. All Bee devices can create conversation summaries and recaps for free, and offer 14 days of memory. With an $11.99 per month Bee Pro subscription, users receive unlimited conversation summaries and integrations with Amazon.com, Alexa+, and third-party applications. Pro users also get suggested to-dos, daily memories, a personal chat assistant, and conversation templates. In addition, you can opt to connect the Bee to Alexa, allowing your Echo device to use its ability to identify your voice, a feature called Voice ID, to recognize when you’re speaking. It can then record your conversations to provide Bee’s insights. (This aspect of Bee is optional, and Amazon notes you can delete transcripts and summaries at any time.) With its new connections to Amazon.com and Alexa, Bee users can make purchases from Amazon or ask Alexa for their Bee insights, summaries, or to-dos hands-free. Bee also works with your existing productivity software, like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Microsoft Outlook, so it can draft emails, set up meetings, surface action items, and more. The Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse both have just one button that turns the device off and on, and include an indicator light when it’s summarizing a conversation. The Frontier also offers IP67 water resistance, up to seven days of battery life, USB-C charging, and dual microphones with advanced noise filtering. All Bee devices come with a companion mobile app, which has also been newly redesigned, plus a new desktop app. The Bee Frontier is available now on Amazon, and the Eclipse will be available soon thereafter. To make all this possible, Bee devices use a private computing security architecture, which doesn’t store the raw audio from your conversations. Instead, audio is processed in real time and then deleted. Transcripts of the conversation are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls, which means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you manually and intentionally share them.

In addition, you can opt to connect the Bee to Alexa, allowing your Echo device to use its ability to identify your voice, a feature called Voice ID, to recognize when you’re speaking. With its new connections to Amazon.com and Alexa, Bee users can make purchases from Amazon or ask Alexa for their Bee insights, summaries, or to-dos hands-free.
Bee also works with your existing productivity software, like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Microsoft Outlook, so it can draft emails, set up meetings, surface action items, and more.

The Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse both have just one button that turns the device off and on, and include an indicator light when it’s summarizing a conversation. The Frontier also offers IP67 water resistance, up to seven days of battery life, USB-C charging, and dual microphones with advanced noise filtering.
All Bee devices come with a companion mobile app, which has also been newly redesigned, plus a new desktop app.
The Bee Frontier is available now on Amazon, and the Eclipse will be available soon thereafter.

extraction.body: Amazon executive Panos Panay has a message for startup founders: Failure is an inevitable, required part of building a successful product. Panay, Amazon SVP of Devices, Alexa, and Leo, shared that advice onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco, drawing on his own experience at Microsoft, where he spent more than 19 years and weathered one particularly expensive failure. “You have to be willing to fail, and actually, not just willing, you actually have to go fail,” Panay said. “If you haven’t failed, you probably haven’t pushed the boundary. It’s literally about harvesting the lessons learned when you fail. You have to be willing to face it, and as you face it, learn from it.” Panay said it’s possible to recover from all sorts of failures, even catastrophic ones, noting that he experienced one himself at Microsoft. He described the launch of the Surface RT, Microsoft’s first tablet computer, as a significant failure during his tenure at the company, one that ultimately led to a nearly $1 billion write-down. “I remember being on the front cover of a newspaper, and it just said failure,” Panay said. “But, here’s the thing, it was easy to admit failure. The trick was, and always is, did you harvest the learnings and understand what happened? All right. What did you learn? Because the failure wasn’t that moment. It was decisions that led up to it two years before that, whether the software wasn’t complete or the inventory was wrong or how we balanced into retail. There were all these steps along the way.” He said founders need to be willing to understand what went wrong, and avoid making excuses, and ultimately accept the failure. “Here’s the other side of it,” he said. “You want to succeed, yeah? You take that failure, but you don’t let go of your vision. That’s it. Surface has done pretty well. You don’t let go of your vision. You don’t break it.” Panay emphasized the importance of staying committed to a vision, learning from experience, and moving quickly. He believes that by embracing failure and learning from setbacks, founders can adapt and make progress faster, even as they encounter new obstacles. “It goes back to the same fundamental, like, have you learned?” he said. “Were you learning along the way? Because if you were learning, then you just change your vector. Usually, it’s not 180 degrees. Usually, it’s just 30 degrees. Take your lessons learned, change a little bit, adapt your vision where it needs to be, and then go. I believe there’s people that hang on too long, but it’s because they haven’t accepted the moment of failure at all.” Aisha is a consumer news reporter at TechCrunch. Prior to joining the publication in 2021, she was a telecom reporter at MobileSyrup. Scope it all out below. Amazon is delivering the first pre-order discounts on Apple’s new HomeView , as we detailed already, but it has also now undercut everyone on the next-generation Apple TV 4K . Amazon is now offering the first discount on Apple TV 4K pre-orders at $289.99 shipped . All of that, combined with the fact that shipping times have slipped significantly at Apple for the new Apple TV 4K – some locations can’t get a pre-order delivered until late November at this point – make this Amazon offer all the more sweeter; Amazon is delivering Apple TV 4K pre-orders faster than Apple and for less now. As of the time of writing, Amazon can still land the new Apple TV on your doorstep on launch day – November 13. This is also true for the new Apple TV Siri Remote (for folks not updating their existing Apple TV unit) and the new HomeView. Delivery times for the new HomeView at Apple are starting to slip into December at this point – Amazon is selling them for less and shipping it on day one still if you’re quick. At some point soon, you’ll be lucky to get a HomeView shipped straight from Apple before December, and the silver model has already sold out at Amazon – you’ll want to get in there quick if you want one: Amazon is still offering a couple colors with an early pre-order discount and shipping them on launch day in mid November, but it’s only a matter of time before they are either completely sold out or tough to get for launch day. As of right now only the Starlight, Space Gray, and Rose Pink are available with launch day delivery on Amazon, and only the latter two are carrying the pre-order discount. Consider this a bit of PSA and get in there now if you plan on getting one at a deal or before December. Just after pre-order discounts went live on the new HomeView , alongside the next-gen Apple TV 4K , Apple’s all-new iPhone Duo is set to go up for pre-order this morning at 8 a.m. ET. You can, of course, get one straight from Apple if you get in there quick, but you might want to explore your options at Best Buy as well – it is offering packages starting at just $55 per month and as much as $1,200 off with trade-ins . As per usual, if you’re looking for a complete unlocked iPhone Duo, you’re going to need to go straight to Apple . However, Best Buy does get competitive with monthly plan options and rates when it comes to brand new iPhone releases and it appears to be doing so for Duo this morning. Best Buy is also offering some trade-in action on the new Duo as well – you can score $1,200 off the total cost of the phone with an iPhone 17 Pro or Pro Max trade, for example. You’ll, of course, want to double check the trade-in value Apple will offer you, but Best Buy can get aggressive with trade-in values as well. These Best Buy iPhone Duo pre-order deals are, admittedly, going to be limited time to some degree, simply because of the carrier options, but they can actually net you the impressive new Apple foldable for much less out of pocket now than paying $2,000+ straight to Apple this morning. We are still tracking a giant $600 price drop on this more pricey 2TB M5 Pro model, but Amazon is now offering Apple’s most affordable 24GB M5 Pro MacBook Pro at the lowest prices in months as well – it is now sitting at $430 off the list. Amazon is now offering the 14-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of RAM and the 1TB SSD down at $2,069.10 shipped with the Space Black livery. This machine carries a $2,499 list price and is now $430 off . We seen this same deal pop up a couple times in the last couple weeks before quickly jumping back up in price, so there’s no telling how long this deal might stick around for. The price we are seeing here today is on par with the lowest we have tracked on Amazon in months. It now joins a pair of particularly notable discounts live on higher-end Pros as well: Apple has officially unleashed the new HomeView smart display and HomePod mini 2 for pre-order, as well as the new, and particularly expensive Apple TV 4K . If you are not ready to drop $299 for the upgraded Apple TV experience, you can at least upgrade your existing setup with the all-new Apple TV Siri Remote (4th generation) for just $59 . No, this is not technically a deal by any means – $59 is the list price on the new Siri Remote. But if history is any indication deals on this thing are going to be incredibly rare and it’s a whole lot less pricey than buying a whole new Apple TV 4K that includes this same remote. The new Apple TV Siri Remote (4th generation) is not only compatible with new Apple TV 4th Gen, but also the Apple TV HD and the previous-generation Apple TV 4K. Alongside pre-orders for the new HomeView smart display , HomePod mini 2 , and Apple TV 4K , this month ushered in all-time low pricing on the 2026 Magic Keyboard you might need for your new M6 Mac mini. And it is still down at the Prime Day all-time low . Considering how rare deals can be at times on Apple’s official Magic accessories, we wanted to highlight this deal on the new all-glyph model once again while it is still live. Regularly $99, you can pick one up over at Amazon down at $79.99 shipped right now. That might not seem like a notable discount, but when it comes to Magic Apple accessories, especially this soon after release, it is. The new HomeView smart display , next-generation Apple TV 4K , and HomePod mini 2 are now available for pre-order, but we are also tracking all-time low pricing across the latest Apple iPhone 18 Pro case lineup . Select models, like the new Olive 18 Pro Silicone case have now dropped again to a new Amazon all-time low at 25% off, and you’ll find loads more with deals below. While most colors and models are still at the Prime Day lows we featured last week, the Apple iPhone 18 Pro Silicone Case with MagSafe in the new Olive colorway has now dropped even lower to $36.75 shipped . That’s 25% off the regular $49 list price and the lowest price we have tracked to date. extraction.body: Earlier this week, Apple announced its new Apple TV 4K, which costs nearly twice as much as the 2022 model did at launch. Amazon is now offering the first discount on the forthcoming streaming box (coming out on November 13th), just days after discounting Apple’s new smart display for the first time. Right now, you can preorder the latest Apple TV 4K ahead of its November 13th release date for $289.99 ($9 off) at Amazon. Unlike its predecessors, though, the new model features far-field microphones so you can quickly make hands-free requests. You can, for example, ask for recommendations, like nature documentaries available on Apple TV, or ask questions about what you’re watching. Siri AI can also understand personal context, too, so long as you have an iPhone or iPad connected to your account that supports Apple Intelligence. Apple has made a few other welcome upgrades, though — as my colleague John Higgins points out — not as many as some may have expected. While Apple skipped features we’d hope to see on a $300 streamer, like audio passthrough and support for 120fps output, it’s nice that the Siri Remote now supports Find My precision tracking, so you can make it ring when it goes missing or use the Find My app on your iPhone to pinpoint its location. The new Apple TV 4K also supports a more expansive surround-sound setup, allowing you to pair up to four compatible HomePod speakers instead of just two. Read our hands-on impressions of the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K. The sale also includes cases for other iPhones, as well as some Samsung and Google phones, so it’s worth browsing even if you’re not planning to upgrade your phone anytime soon. * Fanttik’s S1 Pro electric screwdriver is on sale for $45.99 ($44 off) at Amazon, which is $5 shy of its best price to date. It’s a handy cordless option for small tasks ranging from tightening screws to assembling desks, with 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling a variety of jobs. The USB-C rechargeable screwdriver also comes with a 220RPM motor and three torque settings, along with a LED light to help illuminate your workspace.

extraction.body: Earlier this week, Apple announced its new Apple TV 4K, which costs nearly twice as much as the 2022 model did at launch. Amazon is now offering the first discount on the forthcoming streaming box (coming out on November 13th), just days after discounting Apple’s new smart display for the first time. Right now, you can preorder the latest Apple TV 4K ahead of its November 13th release date for $289.99 ($9 off) at Amazon. Unlike its predecessors, though, the new model features far-field microphones so you can quickly make hands-free requests. You can, for example, ask for recommendations, like nature documentaries available on Apple TV, or ask questions about what you’re watching. Siri AI can also understand personal context, too, so long as you have an iPhone or iPad connected to your account that supports Apple Intelligence. Apple has made a few other welcome upgrades, though — as my colleague John Higgins points out — not as many as some may have expected. While Apple skipped features we’d hope to see on a $300 streamer, like audio passthrough and support for 120fps output, it’s nice that the Siri Remote now supports Find My precision tracking, so you can make it ring when it goes missing or use the Find My app on your iPhone to pinpoint its location. The new Apple TV 4K also supports a more expansive surround-sound setup, allowing you to pair up to four compatible HomePod speakers instead of just two. Read our hands-on impressions of the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K. Three more Verge-approved deals: * If you’ve been meaning to pick up Pikmin 4, Walmart is selling a digital copy for $39.88 ($20 off), which is a great price considering most other retailers are still charging the full $59.99. It’s the original Switch version, but you can upgrade to the forthcoming Nintendo Switch 2 Edition when it arrives on November 12th by purchasing a separate $9.99 upgrade pack, which adds improved graphics and a new Dandori Academy mode. That brings your total to just $49.87, saving you about $20 compared to buying the $69.99 Switch 2 Edition outright. I currently use the OtterBox Symmetry Series Clear Case for my iPhone 16, which normally costs $49.99 but is now available in various colors for just $5.99 with a 90-day warranty. The sale also includes cases for other iPhones, as well as some Samsung and Google phones, so it’s worth browsing even if you’re not planning to upgrade your phone anytime soon. * Fanttik’s S1 Pro electric screwdriver is on sale for $45.99 ($44 off) at Amazon, which is $5 shy of its best price to date. It’s a handy cordless option for small tasks ranging from tightening screws to assembling desks, with 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling a variety of jobs. The USB-C rechargeable screwdriver also comes with a 220RPM motor and three torque settings, along with a LED light to help illuminate your workspace.

Apple ( AAPL ) has danced around making a major push into the smart home market for years, via its HomePod, HomePod mini, and Home app. But it fell shy of ever launching its own dedicated smart home hub, ceding much of the space to Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ). That changed on Tuesday with the launch of Apple's HomeView . Sporting a 7-inch Liquid Retina Display that can sit on a counter or be mounted to a wall, the HomeView serves as Apple's biggest smart home effort to date and could help it win over a market in flux as powerful AI models enter the home . "Most smart speakers and hubs in homes today are low-cost devices that can't run AI at the edge, so they are ripe for replacement," Counterpoint Research research director Mohit Agrawal said in a note following Apple's Welcome Home event on Tuesday. "Amazon and Google have only just begun refreshing their hardware for Alexa+ and Gemini, so the upgrade cycle is wide open, and Apple wants to win it," he added. The HomeView takes a lot of its software design cues from the Apple Watch , complete with a series of built-in clock faces. There's a hub screen that lets you control your smart home devices, such as lights, locks, and thermostats, as well as an iPhone-like home screen where you can open apps like FaceTime or Messages. Users can also view multiple smart camera feeds, use the HomeView's built-in camera as a vanity mirror before they head out the door, and look up things like recipes from their iPhones and then project them on the screen. Apple is framing both its Siri AI and its privacy stance as two key benefits of the HomeView. Siri AI will allow you to control smart home devices with your voice, make FaceTime calls, and ask broad world-knowledge questions. The company designed the HomeView to recognize six faces via its facial recognition camera. If you want to access your personal messages, calendar, and so on, you'll need your iPhone on the same Wi-Fi network as the hub so it can authenticate you. Apple said HomeView does all of this seamlessly, allowing you to simply walk up to it and instantly see your customized home screen and app setup. The new hardware provides users with a long-awaited Apple-built solution for controlling smart home devices. To date, customers have had to wrangle a collection of do-it-yourself options, such as using iPads as wall-mounted command centers. HomeView changes that, with Apple noting that the device will work with existing Apple Home and Matter-compatible accessories . The company has also partnered with LG and Schneider Electr ic to produce new smart door locks, thermostats, and indoor and outdoor cameras. But to win over both Apple loyalists and average users, the company needs to prove that Siri AI is more than just a means to set alarms and check the weather. I've been using Siri AI on my iPhone for the past several weeks, and it's proven to be quite helpful when it comes to asking questions related to texts and emails, such as requesting the name of a restaurant my friend suggested I check out. But I haven't been able to try the AI assistant with HomeView just yet. Whether it works as advertised will be integral to the overall experience. "Generative AI has raised expectations for conversational ease and genuinely useful assistance, and Siri has consistently lagged," Forrester vice president and principal analyst Dipanjan Chatterjee said in a press statement. "The critical question is whether the new Siri capabilities can close that gap and make Apple's home experience as intuitive and compelling as its best products," he explained. If Apple's strategy to take smart home share from Amazon and Google succeeds, it could provide a boost to the company's bottom line while helping to ensure increased lock-in among its customers. Apple doesn't break out specific revenue numbers for its smart home sales, instead lumping them in with wearables and accessories. That segment represented $35.69 billion of the company's $416.16 billion in total revenue in 2025. That's better than its Mac and iPad businesses, but nowhere near its Services division, which brought in $109.15 billion, or its iPhone arm, which generated $209.59 billion in the same period. sources.title: Why Apple is finally making its own smart home devices
passages: For more than a decade, Apple has told other companies to build smart home devices for its platform.
Even after 12 years of HomeKit, Apple’s smart home ecosystem still felt underdeveloped, especially compared to the competition.

Drance says they’ve seen that once people try a single smart device and find it easier than they expected, it “unlocks this delightful understanding of what’s possible once you bring these products into the home.” She argues that most people just don’t know what a smart home can do.

“But sometimes we do get asked, ‘Hey, what product should I put in the home?’” Rather than build devices itself, Apple chose to codevelop the lineup with partners that “have their own expertise in the home.” Both have a global footprint and home experience, she says, “LG more so in consumer products, Schneider through home build and home installations.” Drance says it was a ground-up collaboration with Apple bringing “the design aesthetic that would be suitable for the home and suitable to go with our family of products.” The company is also partnering with ADT through Apple retail stores to help people install the devices.
Does the Home Collection do anything other Apple Home devices can’t?

extraction.body: For more than a decade, Apple has told other companies to build smart home devices for its platform. The Apple Home Collection is a lineup of cameras, thermostats, sensors, a smart door lock, and a video doorbell, all codeveloped with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. They arrive alongside HomeView, Apple’s first smart display. Even after 12 years of HomeKit, Apple’s smart home ecosystem still felt underdeveloped, especially compared to the competition. Amazon’s and Google’s ecosystems support more products, and both have popular in-house brands: Ring and Nest. Apple had nothing of its own to point customers to as an Apple experience — and now it does. And does Apple actually add anything new here, or is this mostly packaging? Drance says the big reason for this focus on new smart home hardware was the development of the right technologies. The second was AI, which brought a more conversational Siri voice assistant. Both were necessary to create a dedicated home device in HomeView. “With the magic of Siri AI, it comes together in a way that we haven’t been able to deliver before,” Drance says. “That’s been a really critical piece of bringing this all together.” The bigger play here is HomeView as a gateway to the smart home for Apple’s users. Buy one for playing music, guided cooking recipes, and checking your calendar, and you might soon want a camera or smart lock to go with it. Drance says they’ve seen that once people try a single smart device and find it easier than they expected, it “unlocks this delightful understanding of what’s possible once you bring these products into the home.” She argues that most people just don’t know what a smart home can do. The biggest barrier to buying smart devices is that people don’t see any value in the products, according to research from Parks Associates. Privacy and security concerns and complexity also rank high, along with cost. While Apple isn’t addressing the cost concern here — the products start at $200 — the other elements are part of its pitch: one-tap setup, your data stays yours, one app to run it all. Apple’s stamp of approval also carries a lot of weight. The Home Collection is more like the chef’s choice, a short list of dishes Apple promises will pair well. “There is a lot of choice with Matter, and there’s a lot of great products out there,” she says. “But sometimes we do get asked, ‘Hey, what product should I put in the home?’” Rather than build devices itself, Apple chose to codevelop the lineup with partners that “have their own expertise in the home.” Both have a global footprint and home experience, she says, “LG more so in consumer products, Schneider through home build and home installations.” Drance says it was a ground-up collaboration with Apple bringing “the design aesthetic that would be suitable for the home and suitable to go with our family of products.” The company is also partnering with ADT through Apple retail stores to help people install the devices. Drance says setup and ease of use were also a big focus in the products’ development. “The one-tap setup was really important to make it so easy, having no need for a separate account, no need for a separate app,” she says. “We just wanted that simplicity to be at its core, and of course, the privacy that we’ve developed together with our partners.” She says everything integrates through Apple Home; you don’t need to create an LG or Schneider account, and all data is end-to-end encrypted, so only you can access it. Drance was clear that the Apple Home Collection isn’t replacing the buffet — the hardware ecosystem that has grown up around Apple Home. “We still have this incredible ecosystem with Matter, and with Works with Apple Home, that is going to remain,” she says. “We know that homes are not a one-size-fits-all solution, so our customers will continue to have that choice, and we remain committed to building that ecosystem as well.” The hardware mostly backs that up. The exception is the cameras, which use Apple’s HomeKit Secure Video, not Matter. I was surprised Apple didn’t announce Matter camera support. But the Thread radios suggest the hardware might be Matter-ready, and Apple may be waiting for the Matter camera standard to support encrypted uploads, something HKSV already does. Does the Home Collection do anything other Apple Home devices can’t? “What we’ve done with Apple Home Collection is we’ve added another layer on top of that, that deeper integration,” says Drance. There aren’t features exclusive to the Home Collection; it’s more that Apple is saying all the features will be here. It’s a bit like Google making a Pixel phone to show Android developers what Android can do: Apple’s products come with the full suite of capabilities the platform offers. The tech giant has been mousy when it comes to smart home tech, but rumors are swirling about an Apple smart home display, security cameras and other home devices ahead of Tuesday's event. Apple’s smart home line is set to arrive in the near future. Here’s what I’m excited about. It’s a matter of when, not if. Apple’s take on the smart home is coming, with multiple reports saying the tech giant is ready to release its own line of smart devices and home security products . While it’s a little early, Apple’s big “awe dropping” event on Sept. 9 could showcase the first elements of its big home expansion. We already expect to see the new iPhone 17 , a new Apple Watch and an AirPod announcement . Here’s what could happen if there’s a surprise home tech release, too, from table robots to home security cameras. Don’t miss any of our unbiased tech content and lab-based reviews. Add CNET as a preferred Google source. How do you create something completely new for the smart home space? The rumor is Apple’s tabletop robot , a smart 7-inch screen mounted to a swiveling arm that can move to face various people sitting around in a living room, kitchen, office or other space. It sounds a bit like Amazon’s swiveling Echo Show 10 (currently discontinued as Amazon appears to be working on an updated model), albeit with an Apple focus on FaceTime for video chats. The “robot” part is largely due to Bubbles, a code name for an updated version of Siri. Apple has been working on several different versions of Siri with more conversational AI features. For the tabletop display, Siri would gain the ability to hold conversations with multiple people at once, and a first-ever animated icon to give Siri a “face” to use in conversations. These new versions of Siri seem to be central to Apple’s smart home plans, but I’m not sure if they’ll see the light of day now that Apple is working on empowering Siri with Google Gemini AI . The robot is ambitious and unlikely to appear at Apple’s fall event. Swiveling smart displays are a tough sell, not to mention mechanical arms, which make displays far more fragile, difficult to use and potentially intrusive. Apple’s smart display could be an expect evolution of its HomePod line. If Apple wants to make a big smart home splash while staying relatively safe and showing off its display prowess (two things Apple loves to do), the fall event may include a smart display . The 7-inch smart display would include many features of the robot, including the bubblier version of Siri, but would stay in one place like most smart displays. Rumors say Apple is focusing on Apple Watch-like widgets and clock faces for such a display, in a new UI labeled Charismatic. Such a screen could serve as a smart alarm clock, home hub or music device, with Siri serving a central role as controller and operator of the display’s various functions. Apple is rumored to release its own security camera after supporting brands like Logitech in the past. With competitors like Amazon’s Ring and Google Nest well-known for their security cameras , it’s no surprise that Apple is considering an entry, as well. According to Bloomberg’s sources , Apple has been experimenting with a variety of camera designs to create a model (code J450, apparently, no snazzy code names here) that can work with the rest of Apple’s smart home. Rumored specs sound familiar to many security cams I’ve tested, including wireless and battery-powered capabilities, plus facial recognition and motion detection. But there’s no firm word on resolution or outdoor capabilities yet. Apple also wants its camera to connect closely with other smart home devices, such as turning lights on and off using its presence-sensing features. An Apple doorbell could compete with models from Nest, ring and more. I’ve heard very little about the possibility of an Apple doorbell, but it fits well with the rest of these rumors. So far, reports only mention that Apple has tested a video doorbell concept . However, it’s one of the easiest entry points into the smart home for buyers and sellers alike, and brands like Nest split their lines into security cams and video doorbells, as well. So even if Apple isn’t quite ready to launch a doorbell yet, I’d bet it happens around the same time as its security camera or soon afterward. I’ll keep you updated on the latest Apple home news, if and when any big announcements hit. For now, take a look at Apple’s competition with my guides to the best smart speakers , best home security cameras and the best security systems . © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All rights reserved.

sources.title: Apple bets its smart home comeback on Siri AI and new smart hub ‘HomeView’ - The Tech Portal
passages: Apple's first smart home hub, HomeView, arrives alongside a refreshed Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini — though Siri AI isn't ready on all of them yet.
All of this is part of the Cupertino giant’s push into creating a complete home devices category.

Apple is entering a smart display category where Amazon and Google have had products for years, and analysts have previously pointed out that the harder problem was never the hardware — it’s getting people to actually wire up a smart home in the first place.

There’s also an irony sitting underneath the entire Siri AI push: Apple has previously confirmed it enlisted Google’s help this year to get Siri’s underlying capabilities up to scratch, meaning the assistant central to Apple’s pitch for its own hardware ecosystem has a rival’s fingerprints on it.

Ternus inherits a company investors have been watching more closely for hardware growth as its services business faces regulatory pressure, and a new product category gives him something fresh to point to.

When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, it can pull in personal context from Calendar, Messages and other apps to give more useful answers, and conversations started on HomeView sync via iCloud so they can continue on an iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch or Vision Pro.

It gets an A19 chip that Apple says delivers up to 50% faster CPU performance and twice the graphics performance of its predecessor, three built-in far-field microphones so people can talk to Siri without touching the remote, and an updated Siri Remote with Find My support and Precision Finding.

Beyond the assistant, HomeView functions as a household command center — FaceTime calls with Center Stage, Intercom, Apple Music with animated lyrics, Apple TV, Apple News and Apple Podcasts, plus control over accessories and scenes from Apple’s new Home Collection accessory line, which adds outdoor cameras, temperature sensors and access management into the same screen.
The Tech Portal is published by Blue Box Media Private Limited .
Our investors have no influence over our reporting.
Read our full Ownership and Funding Disclosure →

HomeView is a 7-inch Liquid Retina display, sold in a tabletop version with a domed aluminium speaker base and stainless steel tilting hinge, and a separate wall-mounted version, both priced at $299 in the US.
It runs on an A18 chip and uses a front-facing camera to recognize up to six different household members by face, switching automatically between a shared household screen and a personalized one.
Pre-orders opened Tuesday, with the device arriving November 13.
Whether that matters to the people actually buying a $299 screen for their kitchen counter is a different question than whether Apple can build one.
Tuesday’s event answered the second question.
The first one plays out over the next few months, starting with how many of these pre-orders convert into shipped November devices.

extraction.body: Apple's first smart home hub, HomeView, arrives alongside a refreshed Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini — though Siri AI isn't ready on all of them yet. Apple made its long-rumored move into the smart home hub category official on Tuesday , unveiling HomeView alongside refreshed versions of the Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini at its “Welcome Home” event in New York. The launch is also a personal milestone of sorts: it’s the first major hardware event for John Ternus, who took over as Apple’s chief executive on September 1 after 25 years at the company, most recently as the executive running hardware engineering. Ternus inherits a company investors have been watching more closely for hardware growth as its services business faces regulatory pressure, and a new product category gives him something fresh to point to. HomeView is a 7-inch Liquid Retina display, sold in a tabletop version with a domed aluminium speaker base and stainless steel tilting hinge, and a separate wall-mounted version, both priced at $299 in the US. The tabletop model comes in silver, starlight, rose pink and space gray, while the wall-mounted version ships in space gray and silver. It runs on an A18 chip and uses a front-facing camera to recognize up to six different household members by face, switching automatically between a shared household screen and a personalized one. Pre-orders opened Tuesday, with the device arriving November 13. The headline feature is Siri AI, an entirely new, more conversational version of Siri built on Apple’s next-generation Apple Intelligence. When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, it can pull in personal context from Calendar, Messages and other apps to give more useful answers, and conversations started on HomeView sync via iCloud so they can continue on an iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch or Vision Pro. Apple’s Greg Joswiak, the company’s senior vice president of worldwide marketing, framed the pitch simply: HomeView is “designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user.” Beyond the assistant, HomeView functions as a household command center — FaceTime calls with Center Stage, Intercom, Apple Music with animated lyrics, Apple TV, Apple News and Apple Podcasts, plus control over accessories and scenes from Apple’s new Home Collection accessory line, which adds outdoor cameras, temperature sensors and access management into the same screen. The new Apple TV 4K, its first update in four years, is a more substantial overhaul than usual. It gets an A19 chip that Apple says delivers up to 50% faster CPU performance and twice the graphics performance of its predecessor, three built-in far-field microphones so people can talk to Siri without touching the remote, and an updated Siri Remote with Find My support and Precision Finding. Apple is also leaning on it as a smart home hub in its own right, using Apple Intelligence to generate camera activity descriptions and summarize notifications inside the Home app. It’s priced at $299, in a single 128GB configuration, and also ships November 13. Bob Borchers, Apple’s vice president of worldwide product marketing, called it the company’s “most immersive home theater experience yet.” The HomePod mini refresh is where the Siri AI story gets more complicated. The new $149 speaker, up $50 from the original 2020 model, gets an S10 chip for better sound and the ability to recognize sounds like a smoke alarm and alert a user’s phone, a feature Alexa devices have had for years. But Apple has confirmed that Siri AI itself won’t be available on the new HomePod mini at launch; it’s coming later through a software update, with no date given. That’s a notable gap in a launch built almost entirely around the promise of a smarter Siri everywhere in the home, and it lands on a different schedule than the rest of the lineup: the new HomePod mini ships October 30, two weeks before HomeView and the new Apple TV 4K. All of this is part of the Cupertino giant’s push into creating a complete home devices category. Apple is entering a smart display category where Amazon and Google have had products for years, and analysts have previously pointed out that the harder problem was never the hardware — it’s getting people to actually wire up a smart home in the first place. There’s also an irony sitting underneath the entire Siri AI push: Apple has previously confirmed it enlisted Google’s help this year to get Siri’s underlying capabilities up to scratch, meaning the assistant central to Apple’s pitch for its own hardware ecosystem has a rival’s fingerprints on it. Whether that matters to the people actually buying a $299 screen for their kitchen counter is a different question than whether Apple can build one. Tuesday’s event answered the second question. The first one plays out over the next few months, starting with how many of these pre-orders convert into shipped November devices. The Tech Portal is published by Blue Box Media Private Limited . coreStoryFacts.text: Apple ( AAPL ) has danced around making a major push into the smart home market for years, via its HomePod, HomePod mini, and Home app.
But it fell shy of ever launching its own dedicated smart home hub, ceding much of the space to Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ).
Apple doesn't break out specific revenue numbers for its smart home sales, instead lumping them in with wearables and accessories.
That segment represented $35.69 billion of the company's $416.16 billion in total revenue in 2025.
That changed on Tuesday with the launch of Apple's HomeView .

Sporting a 7-inch Liquid Retina Display that can sit on a counter or be mounted to a wall, the HomeView serves as Apple's biggest smart home effort to date and could help it win over a market in flux as powerful AI models enter the home .
Apple is framing both its Siri AI and its privacy stance as two key benefits of the HomeView.
Siri AI will allow you to control smart home devices with your voice, make FaceTime calls, and ask broad world-knowledge questions.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Apple said HomeView does all of this seamlessly, allowing you to simply walk up to it and instantly see your customized home screen and app setup.
"The critical question is whether the new Siri capabilities can close that gap and make Apple's home experience as intuitive and compelling as its best products," he explained.
HomeView changes that, with Apple noting that the device will work with existing Apple Home and Matter-compatible accessories .
"Amazon and Google have only just begun refreshing their hardware for Alexa+ and Gemini, so the upgrade cycle is wide open, and Apple wants to win it," he added.
But to win over both Apple loyalists and average users, the company needs to prove that Siri AI is more than just a means to set alarms and check the weather.
For more than a decade, Apple has told other companies to build smart home devices for its platform.
Even after 12 years of HomeKit, Apple’s smart home ecosystem still felt underdeveloped, especially compared to the competition.

Drance says they’ve seen that once people try a single smart device and find it easier than they expected, it “unlocks this delightful understanding of what’s possible once you bring these products into the home.” She argues that most people just don’t know what a smart home can do.

“But sometimes we do get asked, ‘Hey, what product should I put in the home?’” Rather than build devices itself, Apple chose to codevelop the lineup with partners that “have their own expertise in the home.” Both have a global footprint and home experience, she says, “LG more so in consumer products, Schneider through home build and home installations.” Drance says it was a ground-up collaboration with Apple bringing “the design aesthetic that would be suitable for the home and suitable to go with our family of products.” The company is also partnering with ADT through Apple retail stores to help people install the devices.
Does the Home Collection do anything other Apple Home devices can’t?
Every device uses Thread to stay connected if Wi-Fi drops, and Apple says each can update its own network credentials when you change your Wi-Fi.

"“The one-tap setup was really important to make it so easy, having no need for a separate account, no need for a separate app.”" - Kaiann Drance, Apple According to Apple, setup is as simple as tapping your iPhone to the device, like pairing AirPods, with no extra account or app needed and no scanning required.
The biggest barrier to buying smart devices is that people don’t see any value in the products, according to research from Parks Associates.
They arrive alongside HomeView, Apple’s first smart display.
Both were necessary to create a dedicated home device in HomeView.

The tech giant has been mousy when it comes to smart home tech, but rumors are swirling about an Apple smart home display, security cameras and other home devices ahead of Tuesday's event.

I’ll keep you updated on the latest Apple home news, if and when any big announcements hit.
